'''''Dolichandra unguis-cati''''', commonly known as '''cat's claw creeper''', '''funnel creeper''',<ref name=GRIN/> or '''cat's claw trumpet''',<ref name=GRIN/> In Hawai'i it is called '''hug-me-tight'''. is a rapidly growing climbing vine belonging to the family [[Bignoniaceae]].<ref name=BrisRain/> It affects all plant layers of the forest ecosystem spreading rapidly both vertically and horizontally.

==Description==
[[File:Macfadyena_unguis-cati_Flower.jpg|thumb|left|The showy yellow flowers]]
[[File:Μπιγκόνια η ονυχωτή - Bignonia Unguis Cati.jpg|thumb|left|The fruits of ''Dolichandra unguis-cati'' are {{convert|40|–|50|cm|in|abbr=on}} long]]
''Dolichandra unguis-cati'' is a [[liana]] with semipersistent foliage and woody stems that can reach a height of {{convert|30|m}}. Thin and small [[aerial roots]] are used for climbing. Leaves are dark green, opposite and [[Glossary of botanical terms#B|bifoliate]]. Leaflets have a length of {{convert|3|to|4|cm|in|abbr=on}}. Long primary roots extend beneath the soil surface, producing large tubers {{convert|40|–|50|cm|in|abbr=on}} long.<ref name = plantnet>[http://publish.plantnet-project.org/project/plantinvasivekruger/collection/collection/synthese/details/BIGUC#:~:text=Dolichandra%20ungui%2Dcati%20is%20a,or%20greyish%20and%20become%20woody. Plantinvasivekruger - Bignoniaceae - Dolichandra unguis-cati (L.) L.G.Lohmann] Plant Net. Retrieved 25 April 2022.</ref>

Flowers are yellow, have a diameter of {{convert|4|to|5|cm|in|abbr=on}} and can grow alone or in groups of two or three. Flowers occur from late spring through to early summer.<ref>[https://weeds.brisbane.qld.gov.au/weeds/cats-claw-creeper Cat's claw creeper] [[Brisbane City Council]] Weed Identification Tool</ref> Their [[Calyx (botany)|calyx]] is narrow trumpet-shaped, 1–2 centimeters long. Their [[petal|corolla]] is also tubular and measures 4 to 10 centimeters long. The 5 lobes of the corolla have different sizes. The opening diameter is 1.2 to 2.4 centimeters. Fruits are brown flattened capsules from {{convert|25|to|95|cm|in|abbr=on}} long. Each capsule contains 100 to 200 seeds.<ref name = plantnet/>

==Distribution and habitat==
This plant is native to the tropical dry forest of [[Central America]], [[South America]] (Mexico to Brazil and northern Argentina) and the [[Caribbean]]. In these natural areas it occurs from sea level to over {{convert|600|m}} above sea level and where the rainfall is {{convert|750|to|2400|mm|in|abbr=on}} per year. It can become invasive due to its fast growth and it is present worldwide, often having been introduced as an ornamental plant to these regions. It can affect all layers of plants of forest ecosystems by rapidly spreading both vertically and horizontally.<ref name = plantnet/>

It prefers fertile, well-drained soils but can survive in most soils except salty ones. It tolerates the lack of light well, but grows faster in the sun. It is naturalised in Australia, southeastern US, southern Africa, tropical Asia. It grows in orchards and gardens, roadsides and grasslands, in open urban areas, especially in temperate to subtropical regions with medium to high rainfall. It spreads both horizontally, in contact with herbaceous plants, and vertically, up to the [[Canopy (biology)|canopy]].<ref name = plantnet/>

===Invasiveness===
The eradication of this plant is difficult because of its rapid spread linked to the vast [[root system]] it develops and the profusion of its seeds. It survives grazing and [[wildfire]], and disturbances tend to stimulate offspring production. The plant is said to be "one of the most destructive exotic vines", where it is especially aggressive in [[riparian]] zones and rainforest communities where it strangles trees.<ref name = plantnet/>

==Medicinal use==
Its use has been documented as an [[Antivenom|antidote]] for [[snake bite]]s in [[folk medicine]]. It is also used to treat [[dermatitis]], in addition to being [[antipyretic]]. Furthermore, being [[anti-inflammatory]], it has been used for the treatment of intestinal ailments, [[venereal disease]], [[rheumatism]], [[dysentery]], [[malaria]] and [[oliguria]]. Its leaves revealed [[Chemotherapy|antitumoral]] and [[trypanosomes|antitrypanosomal]] activities.<ref>{{cite journal | pmc=2816596 | year=2007 | last1=Aboutabl | first1=E. A. | last2=Hashem | first2=F. A. | last3=Sleem | first3=A. A. | last4=Maamoon | first4=A. A. | title=Flavonoids, Anti-Inflammatory Activity and Cytotoxicity of Macfadyena Unguis-Cati L | journal=African Journal of Traditional, Complementary and Alternative Medicines | volume=5 | issue=1 | pages=18–26 | doi=10.4314/ajtcam.v5i1.31251 | pmid=20162050 }}</ref>
